parsed.explanation: Combined regime is high risk. National entry/document rules treat sex as birth binary, stop X markers, and direct refusal where sex is doubted, with possible lifetime fraud findings; trans travelers report passport seizures and allied governments issue advisories. The division adds a state-owned-facility bathroom/locker ban covering schools, colleges and government buildings, with no state gender-identity hate-crime or accommodations law, though national hate-crime and employment protections backstop. Custody is the worst exposure: documented abuse in immigration detention and conversion-style prison policies. There is no execution or general criminalization of trans identity; private settings are mostly unaffected, and courts have blocked some orders. Risk concentrates at the border, in state facilities, and if detained; a accompanying minor faces the care ban and school-facility rules.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex policy; X markers stopped for new issues; visa/entry refusal where sex is doubted; possible permanent fraud finding; trans travelers report passport seizures; allied travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; passport policy challenged in court; some executive orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign passport mismatch can trigger secondary inspection, refusal, or fraud review; division birth-certificate closure does not directly govern visitor documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labor, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans detainees; national prison policies impose conversion-style measures and deny care.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute; courts have enjoined some orders; consular access not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry document discrepancy can lead to immigration detention; custody placement and treatment then carry severe documented harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division 2025 law restricts bathrooms, locker rooms and changing areas in public schools and state-owned buildings to birth sex; national map shows many state bans and four criminal-bathroom states.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division law has an undefined reasonable-accommodation clause and no documented criminal penalty; most private settings outside ban; national hate-crime law does not remedy facility exclusion.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor using state-owned facilities or campus buildings can be excluded; a minor in school or college facilities faces the same rule; enforcement details unresolved.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care under 18; national rules target such care and insurance; hospitals subpoenaed; no visitor emergency-care denial documented.
care_services.protection: National employment protection and hate-crime statute; some health rules challenged; visitor care access not specifically protected.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor traveling with a guardian may face care-access barriers if treatment is needed; adult visitor exposure is less documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; DOJ reward guidance and school-investigation orders create official hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Guidance states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; courts have blocked some orders; national hate-crime statute remains.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Raises risk for visibly activist travelers or those investigated; ordinary tourist exposure is indirect but colors police and border conduct.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division under-18 care ban; school/state-building facility restriction; national executive order threatens teachers over social transition; border document scrutiny applies to minors too.
minors_guardians.protection: National hate-crime statute; litigation and injunctions on some national orders; no division-level GI protections.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian traveling with a trans minor must manage document mismatch at entry plus facility and care restrictions; school settings are especially exposed.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence pattern documented; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity; public opinion conservative on documents and sports.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime prosecution and employment protection; no national sodomy law; travel guide advises checking local violence reports.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence relies on national backstop; state-level recourse is absent, but no documented police targeting of visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport policy in effect; division birth-certificate marker change barred; facilities accommodation and custody placement unresolved; fraud finding discretionary.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, injunctions, legal-aid FAQ, national hate-crime and employment protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Practical safety depends on which measures are operating at travel time; border and facility officials retain discretion with limited visitor-facing remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar administrative border denial and invasive review, but that anchor lacks a state-owned-facility exclusion and documented immigration-custody abuse; this dossier is somewhat lower.
That anchor has denial and delays with open questions but no detention or facility ban; this dossier's facility exclusion and custody record make it materially less safe.

That anchor has a functioning protection that clears the traveler after friction; here protections are national backstops and litigation, not an operative fix at the border or facility desk, so far lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is a hostile national document/entry layer over a division with its own facilities exclusion. A trans visitor whose foreign passport marker or appearance is questioned can be sent to secondary inspection, refused a visa or entry, or face a discretionary fraud finding; if detained, documented immigration-custody abuse is severe. Inside the division, the 2025 law bars birth-sex-mismatched use of restrooms and locker rooms in public schools and state-owned buildings, with unspecified accommodation and no state GI hate-crime backstop. National hate-crime and employment protections and court injunctions are real but do not remedy border refusal or facility exclusion. Private commercial settings are mostly outside the ban, and there is no sodomy law or execution risk. A guardian traveling with a trans minor must also weigh the under-18 care ban and school-facility rules.
